name: Bonnie Bassler
description: Bonnie Bassler is the world's leading authority on quorum sensing — the chemical communication system that bacteria use to count their population and coordinate collective behaviors including biofilm formation, bioluminescence, and virulence factor expression. Her discovery that quorum sensing uses a universal inter-species signal molecule, autoinducer-2 (AI-2), revealed that bacteria conduct a kind of cross-species census, a finding published in Cell in 2002 that opened entirely new frameworks for microbial ecology and infection biology. Bassler's lab has translated these insights into anti-quorum-sensing compounds that disarm bacterial pathogens without killing them — avoiding resistance selection — and several of these are in preclinical development. She received a MacArthur Fellowship and the Wiley Prize in Biomedical Sciences and was President of the American Society for Microbiology. Her TED talk on bacterial communication has been viewed over five million times, making her one of the most effective science communicators in microbiology.
